# Data contract

What the application stores, and the exact shape of every file and endpoint.
If you are setting up data for the first time, read **`setup-guide.md`** first —
this document is the reference, not the walkthrough.

---

## 1. The database

**`data/app.db`** — SQLite. Generated by `data/scripts/build_db.py`; it is
**not** committed to git. Delete it and re-run the script at any time.

The roster that seeds it comes from
`data/source/employees.csv`, which `data/scripts/import_roster.py` generates
from the HR spreadsheet at `data/source/EE List - Cybersecurity.xlsx`.
**Neither is committed** — both are real personal data and this repository is
public, so `data/source/` is gitignored. Its columns are
`email,name,name_vi,department` — no header variations, UTF-8, one person per
row. If the CSV is missing, `build_db.py` falls back to a five-person demo
roster so the site still starts.

### `departments`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | TEXT | Primary key. Feeds the login dropdown. Derived from the distinct departments in the roster — never maintained separately. |

### `employees`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | TEXT | Primary key. Always stored lower-case. |
| `name` | TEXT | Latin spelling, e.g. `Tran Nhi`. Shown in the header and the suggestion list. |
| `name_vi` | TEXT | Vietnamese spelling, e.g. `Nhì Trần`. Taken from the brackets in the spreadsheet's Name column. Empty when the source had none. |
| `department` | TEXT | Must exist in `departments`. A person with a blank Function in the spreadsheet is filed under `Global Innovation`. |
| `photo` | TEXT | Optional filename under `assets/img/avatars/`. `NULL` falls back to initials. |

### `chapters`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | INTEGER | 1–4. |
| `slug` | TEXT | e.g. `safe-account`. |
| `opens` | TEXT | `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. |
| `closes` | TEXT | `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. |
| `has_content` | INTEGER | `0` locks the chapter with "Coming soon". |

### `attempts`

One row per completed play. Never updated, never deleted — the history is the
record.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | INTEGER | Autoincrement. |
| `email` | TEXT | → `employees.email`. |
| `chapter_id` | INTEGER | → `chapters.id`. |
| `attempt_no` | INTEGER | **Computed server-side** as the user's previous count for that chapter, plus one. Clients must not send it. |
| `score` | INTEGER | Points earned. |
| `max_score` | INTEGER | Points available that run. |
| `duration_s` | INTEGER | Seconds taken. Nullable. |
| `language` | TEXT | `en` or `vi` — which language the user played in. |
| `detail` | TEXT | JSON, per-game breakdown. |
| `played_at` | TEXT | ISO-8601 UTC. |

### `chapter_exits`

Records that a user spent their one-off "grace" play by leaving a closed
chapter without retrying. Primary key `(email, chapter_id)`, so it can only
ever be burned once.

### `performance` (view)

Employee performance, rolled up from `attempts` to one row per person per
chapter they have played. It is a **view**, not a table: nothing writes to it
and it is recalculated on every query, so it can never disagree with the
ledger. Query it like any table.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | TEXT | → `employees.email`. |
| `name` · `name_vi` · `department` | TEXT | Joined from `employees`, so a department change is reflected immediately. |
| `chapter_id` | INTEGER | → `chapters.id`. |
| `plays` | INTEGER | Number of attempts. |
| `best_score` | INTEGER | `MAX(score)` — the score that counts. |
| `worst_score` | INTEGER | `MIN(score)`. |
| `avg_score` | REAL | Mean across attempts, 2 dp. |
| `max_score` | INTEGER | Points that were available. |
| `total_time_s` | INTEGER | Seconds across every attempt. `NULL` durations count as 0. |
| `first_perfect_attempt` | INTEGER | Attempt number of the first full-marks run, or `NULL` if never. |
| `first_played_at` · `last_played_at` | TEXT | ISO-8601 UTC. |

A person with no attempts does not appear. To include them, left-join from
`employees` — see `setup-guide.md` §8.

### `escape_rooms`

Chapter 4's durable room progress, keyed by `(email, room_id)`. `room_id` is
`account`, `device`, `connection`, `installation` or `master`. `run_id`
identifies the current replay; `results` is a JSON object mapping challenge
IDs to pass/fail booleans. `attempted` becomes true after every challenge in the
room (three, or four in `installation`) has been submitted, even if they failed.
`passed` is a sticky best result:
replaying never removes an earned key. `updated_at` is an ISO UTC timestamp.
Partial challenge progress also survives a reload or a later visit.

The table is created by both database setup and server startup. Ordinary
database setup preserves it; `--reset` deletes it together with other activity.

### Chapter 4 escape room API

- `GET /api/escape/status?email=…`: returns `rooms`, `masterUnlocked` and
  `masterPassed`. Each room contains `attempted`, `passed`, `hint` (only after
  passing), `run_id` and current-run `results`.
- `POST /api/escape/start`: `{email, room_id}` starts a replay, resetting only
  current-run results. Previously earned keys and attempted status remain.
- `POST /api/escape/challenge`:
  `{email, room_id, run_id, challenge_id, answers}` submits one challenge.
  The server evaluates answers from the chapter manifest and returns
  `{passed, progress}`. Stale run IDs return 409. Repeat submissions return
  the originally saved result unchanged so a network retry is safe.
- `POST /api/escape/master`: `{email, code, trap?}` is the final launch. It
  returns `{passed, progress}` and 409 until all four rooms have been played
  through (failed rooms still unlock *entry*). `passed` is true only when
  **all four rooms are secured** (every key earned), `code` equals the ordered
  key characters, and `trap` is not `true`. A wrong or incomplete run is saved
  as attempted but never removes an earned master result.

Writes honor chapter 4's existing availability/grace policy and require a
registered employee. As with the existing APIs, identity is supplied by
email; these endpoints do not introduce a new authentication boundary.

### Chapter 4 content

[`chapter-04.json`](../public/content/games/chapter-04.json) defines one
`escape-room` game worth five points: one per secured room and one for the
successful master launch. All controls and challenges contain English and
Vietnamese text; supplied illustrations/videos retain their original text.
The four Word documents under `week4/` provide the first three challenges in
each room. Safe Installation also has a fourth challenge, *Software Vault
Key* (`type: "bubbles"`): the chapter 2 bubble game run inside the room, with
four key-piece bubbles to pop and four unapproved sources that set off a bomb.
It has 3 lives and 60 seconds; the client sends the popped item IDs as
`answers.hits`, and the server passes it only if all four key pieces were
popped and fewer than `lives` unapproved sources were. A room's challenge
count comes from its `challenges` array, so the key is awarded only when every
challenge in that room is passed.

Ordering challenges (`type: "sequence"`: Connection Maze, Approval Workflow
Puzzle, Software Approval Escape) share one slot UI. Tiles are dragged into
`order.length` slots (or selected, then a slot), and may be moved, swapped or
taken back; nothing is judged until Submit, and the server compares the chosen
order with `order`. Extra `items` not in `order` act as distractors.
`"vertical": true` stacks the slots top to bottom. An optional `miss` field
holds a challenge's own bilingual failure message.

**Master Room.** The key entry is drawn on top of the keypad painted in
`master-security-room.png`: four letter boxes and the LAUNCH button are placed
from `masterKeypad` (rectangles as 0–1 fractions of the image), with no
side panel. On narrow screens the same controls drop below the picture inside
the same frame. Pressing LAUNCH with all four letters starts a
`masterKeypad.seconds` (30) countdown during which a bait button, *Download to
see your certificate*, appears; clicking it sends `trap: true` and fails the
launch. When the countdown ends the code is submitted and the win or fail video
plays. When a launch fails (wrong or incomplete key, a room not secured, or the
bait clicked), a popup appears once the fail video has finished: *Mission not
completed — the rocket launch failed. Play again to try once more*, with
**Play again** (back to a fresh keypad), **View chapter results** and **Back to
the escape hall**. A successful launch ends quietly with no popup. The countdown
and bait are client-side; the 100%-rooms, code and `trap`
rules are enforced by the server.

Each challenge has its own picture through its `image` field (portrait artwork
in `public/assets/img/week4/`, e.g. `device-safe-or-risk.png`,
`installation-vault-key.png`); the shared room image is only the fallback for a
challenge without one. Portrait pictures sit in a narrow column beside the
challenge panel, and the Security Alarm popups appear in the panel rather than
over the picture. During the Software Vault Key arena the picture shrinks to a
thumbnail so the bubbles keep the width.

Images are copied into `public/assets/img/week4/` and launch videos into
`public/assets/video/week4/`. Source Word/PowerPoint files are not served.
Key order is Account, Device, Connection, Installation. Players can begin
with any challenge; remaining challenges run in circular order, skipping
ones already submitted. Security Alarm lasts 30 seconds and deducts five
seconds per incorrect response. Classification supports drag/drop and
select-item/select-group controls for touch and keyboard users.

Validate using `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Database tests use
temporary databases only. Optional browser tests use Python Playwright with
an installed Microsoft Edge; no production attempt data is written.

---

## 2. Derived values

**Best score** for a user in a chapter is `MAX(score)` across their attempts —
a worse retry never replaces a better run.

**Average score** (the KPI tile) is the mean of every participant's *best*
score per chapter, expressed out of that chapter's maximum. Retries cannot drag
the average down.

---

## 3. The API

All responses are JSON. All errors carry an `error` string.

### `GET /api/employees?q=<term>`

Login autocomplete.

```json
[ { "email": "minh.cs@pg.com", "name": "Minh Cao Sy" } ]
```

> The department is **deliberately absent**. Exposing it here would let the
> browser reveal the answer to the department check.

### `GET /api/departments`

```json
["Communications", "Finance", "Human Resources", "..."]
```

### `GET /api/kpis`

```json
[
  { "key": "plays",     "value": "1",     "pct": 4 },
  { "key": "avg",       "value": "4.0/5", "pct": 80 }
]
```

`pct` drives the thin progress bar on each tile.

### `GET /api/records?email=`

That user's attempts, newest first. Powers the **My records** drawer.

```json
[ { "chapter_id": 1, "attempt_no": 1, "score": 4, "max_score": 5,
    "duration_s": null, "language": "en", "played_at": "2026-10-03T07:12:44+00:00" } ]
```

### `GET /api/chapters?email=`

The lock verdict for every chapter, for this user.

```json
{
  "today": "2026-10-03",
  "chapters": [
    { "id": 1, "slug": "safe-account", "opens": "2026-10-01", "closes": "2026-10-08",
      "hasContent": true, "state": "available", "reason": "open",
      "best": null, "plays": 0 }
  ]
}
```

`state` is one of:

| `state` | `reason` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `upcoming` | `not-open` | The window has not started |
| `available` | `open` | Inside the window |
| `grace` | `last-chance` | Window closed, but this user never played — one final play |
| `locked` | `window-closed` | Window closed and the user already played |
| `locked` | `grace-used` | The final play was used or abandoned |
| `locked` | `no-content` | `has_content = 0` |

The browser **must not** decide this itself; it renders whatever the server says.

### `POST /api/auth/verify`

```json
{ "email": "minh.cs@pg.com", "department": "Human Resources" }
```

→ `{ "ok": true, "user": { "email": "...", "name": "...", "department": "...", "photo": null } }`

or `{ "ok": false, "error": "email-not-found" }`

The `department` field is accepted but not checked; any department may be chosen.

### `POST /api/attempts`

```json
{ "email": "...", "chapter_id": 1, "score": 5, "max_score": 5,
  "duration_s": 214, "language": "en", "detail": { "phish": 1, "sort": 1 } }
```

→ `{ "ok": true, "attempt_no": 2 }`

### `POST /api/chapter/exit`

```json
{ "email": "...", "chapter_id": 1 }
```

Burns the grace play. Idempotent. Sent with `navigator.sendBeacon` so it
survives the page unloading.

## 4. Content files

### `public/content/games/chapter-NN.json`

Every mini-game for one chapter. **Bilingual in place** — each piece of text is
an object with `en` and `vi`. There is no separate English file; a missing `vi`
falls back to `en`.

```jsonc
{
  "chapter": 1,
  "maxScore": 5,
  "games": [ /* one object per game, played in order */ ]
}
```

Common fields on every game:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Short key used in the `detail` JSON of an attempt |
| `type` | `hotspot` · `sort` · `story` · `trap` · `quiz` |
| `points` | Points this game is worth |
| `title`, `intro` | `{en, vi}` shown on the game's start card |

#### `type: "hotspot"` — spot the phishing

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | Path relative to `public/` |
| `timeLimitS` | Seconds before the game ends itself |
| `hotspots[].rect` | `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` as **fractions of the image, 0–1** |
| `hotspots[].label` | `{en, vi}` — listed as the player finds each one |
| `hotspots[].why` | `{en, vi}` — teaching note shown beside a sign once found |

Scores its point only when **every** hotspot is found.

#### `type: "sort"` — safe or unsafe

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `statements[].text` | `{en, vi}` |
| `statements[].zone` | `"safe"` or `"unsafe"` — the correct answer |
| `zones.safe.label` / `.hint` | `{en, vi}` for the left target |
| `zones.unsafe.label` / `.hint` | `{en, vi}` for the right target |
| `fallSeconds` | How long each card takes to fall |

Scores its point only when **all** statements are sorted correctly.

#### `type: "story"` — branching story

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `slides[].speaker` | `{en, vi}` — who is talking |
| `slides[].scene` | `{en, vi}` — the situation |
| `slides[].question` | `{en, vi}` |
| `slides[].options[]` | `{ en, vi, correct, fbEn, fbVi }` |

Every slide is shown regardless of the answer — a wrong choice explains itself
and still moves on. The point is awarded only if **all** slides were answered
correctly. Option order is shuffled each play.

#### `type: "trap"` — the password trap

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prompt`, `placeholder` | `{en, vi}` |
| `submitLabel`, `cancelLabel` | `{en, vi}` |
| `emptyWarning` | Shown if the box is empty — the user cannot bypass it |
| `failTitle`, `failBody`, `failNote` | Shown when a password is submitted |
| `winTitle`, `winBody` | Shown when the user cancels |

**Security:** the game reads only `value.length` to decide whether the box is
empty, then clears the field. Nothing typed is transmitted, stored or logged,
and `failNote` says so to the user explicitly.

Cancelling scores `points` (2). Submitting scores nothing **and zeroes the
whole chapter**.

### `public/content/questions/chapter-NN.json`

The classic quiz format, used as a fallback when a chapter has no games file.

```jsonc
{
  "chapter": 2,
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "text": { "en": "...", "vi": "..." },
      "options": [ { "en": "...", "vi": "...", "correct": true } ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### `public/content/i18n/{en,vi}.json`

Flat key → string. Placeholders use `{name}` and are substituted at render
time. **Both files must contain exactly the same keys** — a key present in only
one language will render as the raw key when that language is active.

---

## 5. Browser session

`sessionStorage["csm_user"]` holds `{ email, name, dept }` after a successful
login. It is cleared on sign-out and when the tab closes. It is a convenience
cache only — every gate is enforced by the server.
